draft.title: Add `ledger report trial-balance` to the CLI
draft.why: Accountants closing a period fetch the trial balance from the HTTP API with curl and paste it into a spreadsheet. The CLI they already use for `ledger close` has no report command, so the close checklist mixes two tools and two logins.
draft.what:
The Ledger CLI (`src/ledger/cli.py`) gains `ledger report trial-balance --period <YYYY-MM> [--tenant T] [--json]`. It calls the existing reporting service, which reads `v_trial_balance` through the Postgres store. No SQL is added outside `src/ledger/storage/postgres.py`.

Plain output is one line per account: account, debit and credit in minor units. `--json` prints the same object `GET /v1/reports/trial-balance` returns.

Out of scope: no new report types and no change to the HTTP API.

### Behaviour

`ledger report trial-balance --period 2026-08` prints the accounts of that period with their balances and exits 0. An unknown period exits 2 with `error: period 2026-13 not found` on stderr.
acceptance: `ledger report trial-balance --period 2026-08 --json` prints the same JSON as `GET /v1/reports/trial-balance?period=2026-08` for the test tenant.
`ledger report trial-balance --period 2026-13` exits 2 and prints `error: period 2026-13 not found` on stderr.
`test_cli.py::test_report_trial_balance` passes and asserts that no query touches the `entries` table.
context: Reports read from the reporting views (`v_trial_balance`), never from the entries table.
The Ledger CLI is a thin wrapper over the same services the API router calls; `--json` mirrors the API shapes.
The HTTP API serves `/v1/reports/<name>` through the API router.

pack_index.title: Ledger architecture
pack_index.first_line: Ledger is a small bookkeeping web service: a JSON API and a CLI in front of a Postgres store, with server-rendered invoices. Requests flow inward through the la

pack_index.title: API router
pack_index.first_line: Every handler is three lines: parse, call a service, render. Handlers never import Postgres store; see the rules in architecture. Authentication is applied by t

pack_index.title: Auth
pack_index.first_line: Tokens are hashed and looked up in the Postgres store `api_tokens` table. No authorization rules live here; services check permissions.

pack_index.title: Cache helper
pack_index.first_line: Wraps Postgres store reads. Chosen over a Redis sidecar in 0001-postgres-over-sqlite. Services call it through the store facade; nothing above the storage layer

pack_index.title: CSV importer
pack_index.first_line: Matching rules are per tenant and stored in the Postgres store. Each imported entry publishes an audit event on the Event bus.

pack_index.title: Event bus
pack_index.first_line: Introduced by 0003-event-bus-for-audit. Subscribers run after the request's transaction commits, so a failing subscriber never rolls back a posted entry.

pack_index.title: Invoice renderer
pack_index.first_line: Server rendering was decided in 0002-server-rendered-invoices. Reads through the reporting views, never the entries table.

pack_index.title: Ledger CLI
pack_index.first_line: Thin wrapper over the same services the API router calls; output is JSON with --json.

pack_index.title: Postgres store
pack_index.first_line: Chosen in 0001-postgres-over-sqlite. Amounts are integer minor units (see the architecture rules). The Cache helper sits in front of reads.

pack_index.title: Constraints
pack_index.first_line: Non-functional rules every change must keep.

pack_index.title: Conventions
pack_index.first_line: How code in Ledger is written.

pack_index.title: Data
pack_index.first_line: Entries are immutable rows in `entries` (tenant_id, period_id, account, amount_minor, currency, posted_at). Periods close by inserting a `period_close` row; not

pack_index.title: ADR 0001: Postgres over SQLite
pack_index.first_line: Ledger started on SQLite for a single user; multi-tenant hosting needs concurrent writers and row-level tenancy.

pack_index.title: ADR 0002: Server-rendered invoices
pack_index.first_line: Customers download invoices as PDF and view them as HTML; the two must match.

pack_index.title: ADR 0003: Event bus for audit and email
pack_index.first_line: Every service was calling the mailer and writing audit rows inline, so each needed both dependencies.

pack_index.title: Glossary
pack_index.first_line: - **Entry**: one debit or credit line against an account, always part of a balanced posting.

pack_index.title: Interfaces
pack_index.first_line: `/v1/entries`, `/v1/periods`, `/v1/invoices/<id>` and `/v1/reports/<name>`; JSON in and out, errors as `{error: {code, message}}`. Served by the API router.
